# pidginhost_firewall (Resource)

A firewall rules set. Assign it to a server's public interface with pidginhost_server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_firewall" "web" {
  name = "web"

  rule = [
    {
      direction = "in"
      action    = "ACCEPT"
      protocol  = "tcp"
      source    = "192.0.2.0/24"
      dport     = "22"
    },
    {
      direction = "in"
      action    = "ACCEPT"
      protocol  = "tcp"
      dport     = "80,443"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the rules set.

### Optional

- `rule` (Attributes List) Rules of the set. The list is authoritative: rules the set has but the list does not are deleted. A rule is identified by its direction, action, protocol, addresses and ports; changing any of these replaces that rule, while enabled and position change in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the object in the PidginHost API.
- `status` (String) Validation status of the rules: validated, invalid or pending.

<a id="nestedatt--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `action` (String) What happens to matching traffic: ACCEPT, DROP or REJECT.
- `direction` (String) Traffic direction: in or out.

Optional:

- `destination` (String) Destination address: a single IP, a range such as 192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20, or a comma separated list. Unset matches any destination.
- `dport` (String) Destination port: a number, a range such as 80:85, or a comma separated list. Requires protocol.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule applies. Defaults to true.
- `position` (Number) Order of the rule in the set. The API assigns one when left empty.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol, such as tcp, udp or icmp. Unset matches any protocol.
- `source` (String) Source address: a single IP, a range such as 192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20, or a comma separated list. Unset matches any source.
- `sport` (String) Source port: a number, a range such as 80:85, or a comma separated list. Requires protocol.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a firewall rules set by its ID.
terraform import pidginhost_firewall.web 12345
```
